one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-28, before the open [14]. Guidance is $9.3-9.4B of sales and $0.70-0.71 post-split adj EPS [1][11]. Consensus of $0.722 is already above the range [3]. In round 1 I said a Q2 guide miss after the Q1 print caused a 19% drawdown. The supervisor showed that was wrong: the stock closed up 3.2% on the Apr 29 print and only then fell about 20% to $59.60 over three weeks, in an AI-hardware rotation [25]. The last four reactions were +3.6%, -12.2%, +3.2% and +4.5% [25]. So a beat with a small positive reaction is the modal outcome, but the left tail is fat if the Q4 guide or book-to-bill disappoints, as the January beat-and-sell-off showed. Skeptic-side signals for the window: short interest more than doubled to 31.5M shares by Sep 15, though that is still only 1.3% of float [22]; the stock had a 5.7% profit-taking drop on Sep 14 [23]; and it trades close to its $89.26 high. I model a mixture: 70% weight on a 'normal beat' leg centred near $87 with about 11% monthly vol, and 30% on a 'disappointing guide or rotation' leg centred near $82.5 with about 19% vol. That gives a median of about $86, essentially flat (P>=85.67 = 0.515), and a left-skewed spread with overall width near the usual 46%/3.5 = 13%.

fair_value.method: 60% forward P/E plus 40% FCF yield at the Oct-2027 horizon. P/E: NTM EPS of $3.55 x 24x = $85.2. FCF: $3.02/share / 3.5% = $86.3. Blend about $85.5, roughly today's price. Raised from $83 because I no longer lean on UBS's outlier capex forecast.

inputs_detail.derivation: Close to consensus, trimmed only about 1% (I cut 4% in round 1). UBS's +25% 2027 capex growth [8] is the low outlier; Goldman has +54% [19] and Morgan Stanley +29% on cloud capex, or +57-61% on AI capex [20][21]. The small trim keeps some skepticism about the 15% upward revision in 90 days [3] and comms networks being guided down [2].

All three banks see capex growth slowing sharply in 2028: Goldman +12%, Morgan Stanley +14% (hyperscaler plus neocloud), UBS +6%. I take a blend of about 11%, then add operating leverage, CommScope synergies and the non-AI segments to reach roughly 13% EPS growth.
$3.25 x (1 + 0.75 x 13%) = about $3.57, less about 0.5% for Kyber midplane share risk [18], giving $3.55. This is at the low end of the $3.55-3.65 range the supervisor suggested.

Today's multiple is about 25-26x forward [5][3]. GuruFocus [16] and Oakridge [5] both flag APH as overvalued against history. I assume a de-rating of about 1.5-2 turns as organic growth slows from 30%+ toward the mid-teens. I dropped the unsourced '32x to 22x AI-infrastructure median' figure (supervisor), so the multiple now rests on today's multiple less an assumed de-rating for slower growth.
85% conversion of NTM net income ($3.55 x 2,578M = $9.15B). Conversion recovers from about 70% as the working-capital build from acquisition and growth eases [1][7].
Trailing FCF yield is about 1.4% [5]. I assume it normalises to 3.5% as growth slows. That is still a premium yield, justified by an A3/A- credit with leverage below 2x [6][24].
Leverage check only. FCF is levered, so net debt is not subtracted again.

bear.story: 2028 capex growth comes in at the bottom of the range (UBS +6%) and AI orders digest after the 2026 surge, so book-to-bill drops below 1. Foxconn Interconnect takes the major Kyber midplane share for Rubin Ultra, per GF Securities [18]. NTM EPS lands around $3.1 instead of $3.55, and the multiple falls to about 19x. That puts the stock near $59, the 2026 closing floor ($59.60, held twice) and close to Oakridge's $54 intrinsic value.

base.story: Consensus 2027 EPS of about $3.25 is roughly met. 2028 growth slows to low-to-mid teens, in line with Goldman and Morgan Stanley [19][21]. NTM EPS is about $3.55-3.65 and the multiple compresses to 24-25x. A modest gain of about 3%: earnings growth almost fully offset by de-rating.

bull.story: 2027 capex tracks Goldman or Morgan Stanley's AI figures (+54-61%), and Rubin stays all-copper with CPO slipping to 2029 [13]. APH keeps meaningful Kyber content despite the GF report, and CommScope optics adds further upside. NTM EPS reaches about $4.1 and the multiple holds near 28x. Result: about $117.

thesis_break_reason: A sustained close below about $60, which breaks the $59.60 closing floor that held on Mar 30 and May 19 2026 [25], would put APH near 18x my $3.25 2027 EPS. At that point the market would be pricing estimate cuts, not just multiple normalisation. The likely causes are book-to-bill below 1, a lower guide on AI order digestion, a confirmed loss of Kyber share [18], or a hyperscaler capex cut. Both 2026 tests of this level came from rotation and held. A third break would most likely mean something fundamental. Moved from $62 to $60 now that I have the evidenced floor.

Multiple compression as organic growth falls from 30%+ toward the teens. At 26x 2027 EPS, about two-thirds of APH's value is tied to growth beyond current earnings.

Nvidia Kyber/Rubin Ultra content share. GF Securities says Foxconn Interconnect may have displaced APH as the major midplane supplier [18]. It is a single sell-side report, apparently from about March 2026, and the strong Q2 that followed suggests it has not yet shown up in numbers.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor showed three of my round-1 bear inputs were weak. (1) The post-Q1 drawdown was not caused by a guide miss: the stock rose 3.2% on the print, then fell about 20% over three weeks in an AI-hardware rotation [25]. Tickeron [9] is discounted. (2) The '32x to 22x AI-infrastructure P/E' figure is not in the Yahoo article [8], so I dropped it. (3) UBS's +25% 2027 capex growth is the low outlier. I checked: Goldman has +54% in 2027 and +12% in 2028 [19], and Morgan Stanley has +29% on cloud capex, or 57-61% on AI capex, with 14% in 2028 [20][21]. So I removed most of my 4% skeptic cut to 2027 EPS ($3.15 to $3.25) and raised horizon NTM EPS from $3.45 to $3.55. I keep that below the $3.6 a straight consensus roll implies, because every bank sees 2028 capex growth collapsing to 6-14% and because of the Kyber risk. New skeptic evidence: GF Securities (Alicia Xi) says Nvidia may have replaced APH with Foxconn Interconnect as the major Kyber midplane supplier [18]. I could only reach headlines, which date it to about March 2026, so it predates the strong Q2 and may be partly priced. Still, Kyber ships with Rubin Ultra inside the horizon, so I keep it as a left-tail driver and as part of the bear scenario. Other in-lane checks: short interest rose 132% to 1.3% of float [22], insiders sold steadily [22][4], and a 5.7% profit-taking day came on Sep 14 [23]. Credit remains a non-issue: S&P A-, leverage below 2x [24][6]. I found no accounting or litigation flags. Valuation: P/E $85.2 and FCF yield $86.3 blend to a fair value of $85.5, up from $83. Scenarios are $59 / $88.5 / $117 at 25/50/25, for a mean of about $88. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals around those scenarios (vols of 22% / 17% / 17%), with about 6% of the mass in fat-tail components at $45 and $140 so ±40% one-year moves stay plausible against 46% realized vol. P(>=86) moves from 0.495 to 0.525. P(>=129) moves from 0.075 to 0.09: the supervisor said my upper tail was the thinnest in the group, and the Goldman and Morgan Stanley figures make a bull case more plausible. Even so, I keep a left tail at least as heavy as the group's (P>=60 = 0.838). Disagreements with the supervisor: I keep the fair value at $85.5, below its $89, because I weight the 2028 capex cliff and the de-rating risk more heavily. I also treat the GF report as older and partly priced, so it gets less extra tail mass than a brand-new finding would. Limits: the Intellectia pages returned 403, so the GF report's details and date come from search snippets only. I did not re-pull daily closes myself; the reaction figures are the supervisor's Twelve Data verification [25].
